note: Questions are written once, with their evidence, and never edited; only the result is added after the window closes. Scored with the Brier score against a 50% benchmark (0.25). The git history of this file is the audit trail.

methods.poisson-persistence-v1: Used until 19 October 2026. Counted any word in the headline or summary and assumed this week's rate would fade slightly. It picked up ordinary words such as 'firm' and 'service', which are steady every week. Its questions are kept and scored.
methods.indicator-v1: From 20 October 2026. Questions about real outcomes in the economy, jobs and research, settled from public data (FRED, Eurostat, arXiv). Each is first tested on the full history of its series. Where the method shows no skill over the long-run rate of the event, the probability is pulled back to that rate.
methods.burst-persistence-v2: From 19 October 2026. Terms come from headlines only. A phrase counts as emerging only when it is used at least 2.2 times as often as in the previous three weeks, in at least 5 stories from at least 3 outlets (4 for research-only phrases). Probabilities are corrected using how often comparable phrases held their level in the weeks already collected. Phrases still confined to research sources get a different question: will they reach tech or business coverage?
